hypotheses.claim: Existing ClayCode CapabilityToken and EffectIntent semantics can lower on Ubuntu to opaque host capability handles plus Linux-enforced resource/verb views without a ClayCode semantic change.
support: Local Linux namespace/chroot/read-only-bind experiment enforced read-only resource access and denied ambient paths.
WASI runtime-capability design independently uses unforgeable handles for resource authority.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: ClayCode needs new language-level OS-specific authority primitives for Ubuntu.
hypotheses.falsifier: A required Frank v0.1 Ubuntu effect cannot be represented and securely lowered using current capability/effect semantics plus typed host adapters without semantic leakage or an untestable escape hatch.
hypotheses.next_test: Implement the first real ClayCode Ubuntu capability lowering in the compiler/runtime and execute APP-08 on the developer Ubuntu system.

hypotheses.claim: For Frank v0.1 on Ubuntu, a layered effect sandbox using explicit resource handles/mounts plus Ubuntu-native confinement is more robust than depending on any one Linux sandbox API.
support: Landlock returned ENOSYS in the current Linux execution environment while user+mount namespaces worked.
Ubuntu documents AppArmor as a default LSM confinement mechanism.
hypotheses.counterhypothesis: Landlock alone is sufficiently universal for the v0.1 effect gateway.
hypotheses.falsifier: Developer Ubuntu validation shows one backend has complete required coverage, stable availability, lower complexity, equivalent isolation and better recovery across all mandatory APP-08/FRANK effect classes.
hypotheses.next_test: Probe AppArmor, Landlock ABI, unprivileged user namespace policy, seccomp/no_new_privs and namespace isolation on the exact developer Ubuntu host.

hypotheses.claim: Capability metadata alone, without an OS/runtime enforcement layer, is sufficient to prevent ambient Linux authority.
hypotheses.counterevidence: Unsandboxed baseline retained ordinary filesystem access including /etc/passwd despite no ClayCode capability grant.
hypotheses.meaning: Semantic capability records are necessary for reasoning/audit but are not enforcement by themselves.
